question: Under the MTP (Amendment) Act 2021, which category of women is eligible for termination of pregnancy up to 24 weeks gestation with the opinion of only TWO registered medical practitioners?

answers.text: Women who request termination due to contraceptive failure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Contraceptive failure is a ground for MTP up to 20 weeks with one RMP opinion under the 2021 Act. The 24-week threshold with two RMPs applies to specific vulnerable categories.

answers.text: Survivors of sexual assault, rape, or incest

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The 2021 Amendment extended eligibility up to 24 weeks (with two RMP opinions) for survivors of sexual assault/rape/incest, minors, women with physical or mental disabilities, and foetal abnormalities incompatible with life.
Marriage is no longer a criterion under the 2021 Amendment — the Act was amended specifically to remove this restriction. Eligibility up to 24 weeks is limited to defined vulnerable categories.

answers.text: Women with foetal abnormalities detected at any gestational age

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Foetal abnormalities incompatible with life can be a ground for late termination via the Medical Board (>24 weeks), but foetal abnormalities per se do not automatically qualify a woman for the 24-week two-RMP provision.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the MTP Amendment Act 2021. The 24-week provision with two-RMP opinion applies to specific vulnerable groups, not to all women or contraceptive failure cases.

Well done. The 2021 Amendment created a two-tier system: up to 20 weeks (one RMP) and up to 24 weeks (two RMPs) for specific vulnerable categories including rape/incest survivors, minors, and women with disabilities.
